subject: EU processing evidence request — SCCs / attestation and retention guarantees
messages:
From: Elena Novak <elenan@medicushealth.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: EU-only processing and SCCs — evidence for security & procurement

Hi Connor / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and security at Medicus have a couple of hard requirements before we can move to legal review: any customer data (requests, logs, embeddings) must be processed and stored only in EU jurisdictions, and we need confirmation that SCCs are in place post-Schrems II with any relevant subprocessors.

Specifically, our security team is asking for:
- A copy of executed SCCs (or confirmation we can sign an EU addendum)
- Evidence that the data plane is EU-only (data flow diagram + list of Regions)
- Retention / deletion policy and a description of deletion primitives (API / console flow)
- Confirmation about whether Redwood personnel or support contractors in the US can access customer data or logs

Procurement has a hard deadline — we need those artifacts by 26 Jul to keep the procurement window open. Can you confirm what you can provide and a delivery ETA?

Best,
Elena Novak
Head of Security — Medicus Health
elenan@medicushealth.com
+44 20 7123 9988

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <elenan@medicushealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: EU-only processing and SCCs — evidence for security & procurement

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list and the deadline. Looping in our privacy lead (Soojin Lee) and Marissa from Solutions so we can assemble the right artifacts.

Quick summary of options we can offer immediately:
1) Redwood Private (VPC / customer-managed networking) — data plane and control plane can be isolated to an EU region and run under the customer's network controls. This is the safest route for strict EU-only commitments.
2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity in an EU region) — data plane in EU; our control plane remains multi-region but we can provide tighter access controls and audit logs.
3) Hosted API (standard) — default case where some control-plane operations and support tools may touch metadata outside EU; not recommended if the requirement is absolute EU-only processing.

For the artifacts you requested, we can prepare:
- Executed SCCs (PDF stub attached) and our DPA / subprocessors list.
- EU data flow diagram showing data plane locations and where logs/metrics are stored (attached).
- Retention and deletion playbook: tokens & request logs default retention, customer-initiated deletion API, and support-assisted deletion steps.
- A short attestation letter we can sign committing to EU-only processing for the data plane under Dedicated/Private deployments.

Outstanding points we need to confirm with Legal/Infra (I will escalate):
- Whether any support or SRE escalation path requires emergency access from US-based staff for the Dedicated/Hosted control plane (we will document escalation controls and audit trails).
- Exact retention windows for telemetry vs. raw request logs for the Dedicated option (I believe default logged material is retained 90 days; will confirm).

Can you confirm if Medicus needs: (A) legal-level executed SCCs signed by Redwood, or (B) permission to sign our standard SCCs / addendum? That affects how quickly we can provide the redline.

I will aim to get a draft evidence bundle by Friday (24 Jul). If that works, we can schedule a technical call on 25 Jul to walk your security team through the artifacts.

Thanks — Connor

Team — forwarding Elena's note. Procurement timeline is real; if we want to keep this expansion opportunity open we need to be decisive. Suggested immediate plan:
- Produce a "Medicus evidence bundle" that includes: executed SCCs (or a signable addendum), DPA, subprocessors CSV, EU dataflow diagram, attestation letter, SOC2 excerpt, and clear retention/deletion steps.
- Recommend pushing Private or Dedicated for the initial deployment; Hosted only if Medicus accepts our documented control-plane constraints.
- Ask Legal to prepare a one-page attestation and confirm who on our side is authorized to sign SCCs.

I'll prep procurement-facing language for deal intake and confirm whether sales discounting or credits are needed to move the pilot.

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:12:00 +0200
Subject: Re: EU-only processing and SCCs — technical/legal clarifications

Connor / Kim / Marissa —

Below are concrete answers we can provide to Medicus now and what requires legal sign-off. Please use this copy in the attestation bundle.

1) SCCs and DPA
- Redwood has executed the EU Standard Contractual Clauses with our legal entity; an executed PDF can be attached. For customers that require it, we also offer the option to sign our standard SCC addendum (legal review may take 3-5 business days).

2) Data plane / control plane separation
- Private: control plane and data plane are configurable to run entirely within EU regions; keys and customer data remain in-customer EU tenancy if they select our on-prem/key-management options.
- Dedicated: data plane (model inference, request logs) is hosted in EU regions. Our control plane (orchestration, billing metadata) is geographically distributed; access controls are audited and we can scope admin accounts by region and role.

3) Subprocessors and support access
- Current subprocessors that store/process customer data are listed in the attached CSV. We use EU-region object storage for Dedicated/Private; however, support tooling may surface metadata to a management plane.
- Emergency escalation: US-based support may be engaged only under documented escalation playbooks with RBAC, time-limited access, and full audit logging. We can include this in the evidence bundle.

4) Retention & deletion
- Request logs & observable telemetry: default retention 90 days for Dedicated/Hosted; can be reduced via config for Private deployments.
- KV cache / ephemeral token caches: short-lived (default 1–2 hours); not retained beyond session unless customer enables longer-term caches.
- Customer-initiated deletion: REST API endpoint + console flow; we will document the exact API path and sample commands. Delete actions generate an audit record and a deletion timestamp.

5) Evidence artifacts we will produce
- Executed SCCs (PDF stub)
- DPA and subprocessors list (CSV stub)
- EU-only dataflow PNG (attached)
- Short attestation letter for Dedicated/Private EU-only data plane
- SOC2 summary & pointer to full SOC2 report (we can redact if needed)

Next steps (for this thread):
- Connor to confirm whether Medicus wants Redwood to execute SCCs or Medicus will sign our standard addendum.
- Legal to prepare one-page attestation + provide timeline for SCC signature (3–5 business days if redline).
- Marissa to schedule a technical walkthrough for 25 Jul (aim for 09:00–10:00 CET).

Soojin Lee
VP, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Two quick clarifications:
1) Can Redwood provide a signed attestation committing that Redwood personnel based in the US will not access customer request payloads or raw logs for Dedicated/Private deployments?
2) Can you confirm the exact API path for customer-initiated deletion so we can include it in our procurement pack?

We still need the bundle by Mon (26 Jul). If Redwood can commit to an attestation and SCC PDF by 24 Jul, we can keep the procurement timeline.

Best,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the clarity and the preferred approach. Committing to the plan:
- Redwood legal will provide an executed PDF of the SCCs (or confirm signature) and a one-page attestation stating that, for Dedicated and Private EU deployments, the data plane is processed and stored only in EU regions and that US-based personnel will not access raw request payloads or raw logs except under documented emergency procedures (time-limited, audited). We will keep the attestation scope narrow and operational.
- We will include the exact deletion API endpoint and a sample curl snippet in the evidence bundle.
- Target: deliver full evidence bundle (SCCs PDF + attestation + DPA + subprocessors + dataflow + deletion API) by Fri, 24 Jul.

I will schedule a 25 Jul walkthrough for your security + engineering teams; Marissa will send a calendar invite. If anything changes on Redwood's side we will escalate immediately.

Regards,
